turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - alloy_pair_max_train.csv: 300 samples described by composition in wt% — C, Mn, Si, Cr, Ni, Mo, V, Nb, Co, Al, Ti, Cu
      (Fe is the balance: Fe = 100 − Σ of the others) — plus processing parameters
      (solutionizing_temp, aging_temp, aging_time, cooling_rate) and categorical
      settings heat_treatment (annealed | quenched | quench_temper | solution_aged)
      and route (cast | wrought | AM), with the measured 0.2 % proof yield strength in MPa (the `target` column).
  - alloy_pair_max_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE recipes whose yield strength was NOT measured, with the same columns plus `candidate_id` and no `target`.

Using the training data, predict which candidates have the HIGHEST yield strength (MPa), then select the 5 best candidates from the pool.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
## Analysis of the training data

**1. Heat treatment & route dominate.** Sorting the training set by target shows the top ~20 samples (610–713 MPa) are overwhelmingly `solution_aged` + `wrought` (with a few `solution_aged`/`quench_temper` + `AM`). The bottom of the distribution (100–260 MPa) is dominated by `annealed` and, to a lesser extent, `quenched` samples. Rough group means: solution_aged ≫ quench_temper > quenched > annealed; wrought > AM > cast.

**2. Composition trends among the winners.** The strongest alloys look like maraging/precipitation-hardened steels: low-to-moderate C (< ~0.6), Ni ≈ 5–15, Mo ≈ 1–4, Co ≈ 3–10, modest Ti/Al, moderate Cr. Very high C (~1.2), Cr = 22, Mo = 6, or Al = 2 combined with annealed/quenched treatments consistently give low strength (Al/Ti only "pay off" when solution_aged, i.e., when precipitates can form).

**3. Processing among the winners.** Aging temperature ~600–740 °C with solution_aged/wrought is where the 620–713 MPa samples cluster (e.g., 712.9 MPa: Ni 13, Mo 3.0, Co 6.8, aged 706 °C; 697.9 MPa: Ni 4.7, Mo 3.5, Co 8.8, aged 702 °C; 676.7 MPa: Cr 11.7, Ni 12.5, aged 641 °C; 668.2 MPa: Cr 8.4, Ni 6.6, Mo 2.9, aged 635 °C).

## Matching pool candidates (nearest-neighbor reasoning)

- **c072** (solution_aged, wrought; C 0.32, Ni 9.3, Mo 2.7, Co 7.4, aged 750 °C) — near-clone of the 697.9 MPa training sample. Predicted ~680–700.
- **c008** (solution_aged, wrought; C 0.45, Ni 13.0, Mo 3.9, Co 8.4, aged 683 °C) — closely matches the 712.9 and 648.6 MPa samples. Predicted ~650.
- **c053** (solution_aged, wrought; C 0.16, Cr 16.3, Ni 12.4, aged 730 °C) — analogous to the 676.7 and 628.6 MPa samples. Predicted ~620–650.
- **c021** (solution_aged, wrought; C 0, Cr 13.4, Ni 7.7, Mo 1.3, Ti 1.0, aged 592 °C) — matches the 668.2 / 591.4 MPa neighborhood. Predicted ~600–630.
- **c033** (solution_aged, AM; C 0, Cr 9.1, Ni 11.0, Co 7.6, aged 640 °C, fast cooling) — matches the best solution_aged AM samples (637.6, 619.4 MPa). Predicted ~610.

Runner-up: c038 (solution_aged wrought, ~590–600); other quench_temper/quenched candidates (c028, c050, c083, c091) project to only ~500–540 MPa.

**Final: c072, c008, c053, c021, c033**
